Theme portrait · research pilot [scope-97]

Portrait: formal

What makes Formal Formal, drawn on the package's real stylesheets and components and fixed to this theme. Every word, role and verb comes from themes/formal/signature.json, and every claim there cites the token, selector or keyframes that proves it; tests/theme-portraits.spec.mjs refuses a citation the stylesheet does not contain. Each of the nine sections is a block with its own verdict. A row or verb marked Open is a proposal for Kenny, not a fact about the theme.

1 · Idea

Look at: the idea is at most three sentences, and the list under it is what may not move. Read each claim against the rest of this page: every later section should be explainable from these lines, and a claim that nothing below shows is a claim to strike. Each claim carries its proof, the token, selector or keyframes in formal's own files that make it true.

Paper and ink: a warm off-white stock, near-black ink with a blue cast, and one navy that carries every interactive thing, with bronze and gold as a second voice that never acts. Fraunces on the headings is the whole typographic gesture. Formal stays still while the others move: motion commits once, as a fade, a rise or a rule that draws, and never glitches, loops or flickers.

  1. The ground is a warm off-white; moved to pure white, the theme becomes light.

    Proof
    • themes/formal/tokens.json --background

  2. One colour acts: navy is the only hue that means you can do something here.

    Proof

    • css/formal-register.css [data-theme='formal'] .kp-nav__link--cta
    • css/formal-register.css [data-theme='formal'] .kp-button--ghost

  3. No ornament: no glow, no visible texture, no flourish; the 0.375rem radius is the largest concession.

    Proof
    • themes/formal/tokens.json --radius
    • css/formal-register.css [data-theme='formal'] .kp-card

  4. The display serif is for headings only, at its highest optical size on a surface.

    Proof
    • css/formal-register.css [data-theme='formal'] h1
    • css/formal-register.css [data-theme='formal'] [data-kp-surface] h1

  5. Motion commits, it does not perform: every reveal is a one-shot transition and the register has no keyframes.

    Proof
    • css/formal-register.css --kp-reveal-headline
    • css/formal-register.css [data-theme='formal'] [data-kp-reveal='headline']

2 · Colour in its role

Look at: 10 roles, each a swatch of its token as the page resolves it, what the role may carry, what it may never carry, and a live component using it. The swatch and the component must show the same colour. Then read across the cards: a colour that appears in a component under a role it is told never to take is a finding. Roles in formal: Paper, Card stock, Ink, Navy, Bronze wash, Gold signal, Brick, Rule, Hairline, Muted stock.

4 · Shape

Look at: the corners, the edges and what floats. Radius, borders, shadows, and last the one shape this theme is recognised by. Every example is the component as it ships; check that its corner, edge and shadow are the ones the sentence above it describes, at this zoom and at 200 %.

Radius

0.375rem on buttons, cards, fields and panels; 2px less on badges and tabs; 3px on the stamp. Status dots, timeline markers and the chosen day are circles and the switch is a pill.

5 · Surfaces

Look at: each ground with the same card and the same two buttons on it. On every ground the card must read as raised in this theme's own way, the primary button must be the loudest thing, and no text may sink into its ground. The hero remaps the tokens (AR38): a button on the hero is not the button on the app surface, and should not look like it.

6 · Motion

Look at: first the live copies above the stage. Each verb has a Replay button that plays the register's own rule on a real component: hover and press are the register's :hover and :active rules applied by the page, not a copy of them. Then switch Reduced motion on and replay each again: what is left must be exactly the column "Reduced motion" in the table. Flicker in formal: not allowed, Formal commits to a line once: no glitch, no decipher, no loop. The headline stays whole from the first frame to the last, and the register holds no keyframes at all. Marked open, a proposal rather than a fact: attention.
For every copy below

Follows your system setting until you press it; the page rewrites its own motion guards, so the stylesheets decide what remains.

8 · Voice

Look at: how formal talks: its case, the small words and prefixes it puts in front of things, how it draws instead of using icons, and what it never does. The sample under the list is real markup; every rule in the list should be visible in it.
Case
Sentence case for headings, buttons and links; spaced capitals only for the masthead line, footer headings and the stamp; small caps for the band and menu captions.
Labels
  • A microlabel is a masthead line in navy capitals.
  • A field label is the ink at weight 600, with no prefix.
  • The stamp reads the consumer's own label and never swaps it on reveal.
  • Footer links and the language link underline only under the pointer.
Icons
Almost none: laurel glyphs take the gold, and status dots and timeline markers are plain circles.
Never
  • Pure white paper or pure black ink.
  • Bronze or gold on something that acts.
  • A visible texture, a glow or a rounded flourish.
  • A serif in running text.
  • Touch the headline's characters, or loop a reveal.

Worked example: a banner that asks for attention

A banner that asks for attention, from existing parts only: a card on the page with a masthead line, a Fraunces title, the warning alert whose word 'Warning:' carries the meaning, the navy button with its gold impression beside a ghost button, and the docket cut under it. No stamp: on a card without a dossier reveal the stamp has nothing to anchor to (see the README).

Parts used: .kp-alert .kp-alert--warning .kp-alert__body .kp-alert__icon .kp-alert__label .kp-button .kp-button--ghost .kp-button--mirror .kp-button--primary .kp-card .kp-card__body .kp-card__header .kp-card__title .kp-row .kp-section .kp-stack .microlabel; hooks data-kp-divider data-kp-semantic data-kp-surface.
